data.title: PG&E Makes History as First Energy Utility to Earn International Emergency Management Accreditation | PCG Stock News
data.description:

Independent assessment validates emergency preparedness for a utility serving more than 16 million Californians

OAKLAND, Calif., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) has become the first energy utility in the world to earn accreditation from the Emergency Management Accreditation Program (EMAP), an independent, internationally recognized third-party organization.

The accreditation validates PG&E's emergency management capabilities across preparedness, response and recovery—essential responsibilities for a utility serving more than 16 million customers in Northern and Central California.

According to EMAP, in order to earn accreditation, organizations must demonstrate compliance with all 73 emergency management standards. PG&E met those standards with zero nonconformances identified during its assessment, demonstrating that its emergency policies, plans and practices meet EMAP's requirements.

PG&E joins only three other private-sector organizations in earning EMAP accreditation. Other accredited organizations include Amtrak and the District of Columbia Water & Sewer Authority.

As part of a five-year effort to earn EMAP accreditation, PG&E benchmarked against other accredited organizations, participated in external accreditation assessments and strengthened its emergency policies and procedures. The effort also built on PG&E's existing process for reviewing and improving how it prepares for, responds to and recovers from emergencies.

"When an emergency happens, our customers and communities need to know we're ready to respond quickly and effectively," said Angie Gibson, PG&E's vice president of emergency preparedness and response. "This accreditation confirms our program measures up to the highest standards in emergency management, and it reflects the years our teams have spent raising the bar for how we protect the people we serve."

Meeting rigorous emergency management standards

EMAP's voluntary, peer-reviewed assessment examines how organizations identify hazards, assess risks, plan for emergencies, manage incidents, coordinate resources and communicate with the public. It also evaluates training, exercises and recovery capabilities, looking beyond written plans to the broader emergency management program.

EMAP-accredited programs span state, local and international emergency management organizations, as well as a small number of organizations outside traditional government emergency management agencies. PG&E's accreditation extends that reach to the energy utility industry for the first time.  

"There were so many things that stood out about PG&E far beyond simply meeting the standards," said Jody Ferguson, chair of the EMAP commission and a former county emergency-management director. "They understand that emergencies are ultimately about people—the communities they serve and the employees who support them—and you could feel that commitment throughout the organization."  

PG&E's commitment to emergency preparedness extends beyond its own operations. Customers can find resources to help prepare for emergencies and stay informed, including tips on building an emergency supply kit, at PG&E's Safety Action Center web page.  

About PG&E 
Pacific Gas and Electric Company, a subsidiary of PG&E Corporation (NYSE: PCG), is a combined natural gas and electric utility serving more than 16 million people across Northern and Central California.

KANSAS CITY, Mo., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kansas City Life Insurance Company recorded net income of $1.7 million or $0.18 per share in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $2.8 million or $0.29 per share in the third quarter of 2025.  The decline in net income in the third quarter of 2026 reflected a $1.1 million or 1% decrease in insurance revenues and a $0.6 million or 1% decrease in investment revenues compared to the prior year.  These were partially offset by a $0.8 million or 3% decrease in operating expenses versus the prior year. 

Net income totaled $19.1 million or $1.97 per share in the first nine months of 2026 compared to a net loss of $21.7 million or $2.24 per share in the first nine months of 2025.  The primary factor for the increase in net income in the first nine months of 2026 was lower operating expenses compared to the prior year.  A legal settlement accrual of $35.5 million, net of tax, related to class action lawsuits, was established in the second quarter of 2025.  Excluding this legal settlement accrual, net income would have been $13.8 million or $1.43 per share in the first nine months of 2025.  After excluding the legal settlement accrual, net income for the nine months of 2026 would have been $5.3 million or 38% higher than the prior year, largely due to a $4.7 million or 4% increase in investment revenues. 

Kansas City Life Insurance Company (OTCQX: KCLI) was established in 1895 and is based in Kansas City, Missouri.  The Company's primary business is providing financial protection through the sale of life insurance and annuities.  The Company operates in 49 states and the District of Columbia.  For more information, please visit www.kclife.com.

High school seniors are encouraged to apply for Edison International's $1.5 million STEM scholarship program.

ROSEMEAD, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--High school seniors with dreams of shaping the future can now apply for a $50,000 scholarship to pursue a college degree in STEM through the Edison Scholars program. Starting today, the program is accepting applications from students ready to take the next step toward a future in science, technology, engineering or math.

Since 2006, Edison International has awarded more than $22 million in scholarships to 850 students. Alumni of the program have gone on to build careers across STEM, including computer science, civil engineering and environmental science — helping strengthen communities and powering progress.

Designed to develop the next generation of innovators, thinkers and problem solvers, the Edison Scholars program awards scholarships, paid over four years, to 30 high school seniors across Southern California Edison’s service area each year. Scholarship recipients can also apply for a paid summer internship with SCE after completing their first year at an accredited four-year college or university.

“Developing the next generation of STEM talent starts with creating opportunities for young people who are ready to make a difference,” said Pedro J. Pizarro, president and CEO of Edison International. “The Edison Scholars program helps students pursue their education and build careers that will strengthen their communities and California’s future.”

Applicants must be high school seniors, live in SCE's service area and plan to enroll as full-time undergraduate students majoring in a STEM field in the fall of 2027. Students must have a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 and a demonstrated financial need. First-generation college students are encouraged to apply.

The deadline to apply for the Edison Scholars program is Jan. 21, 2027. Eligible students can apply at edisonscholars.com. Scholarship recipients will be announced in spring 2027.

The Edison Scholars program is fully funded by Edison International shareholders.

About Edison International

Edison International (NYSE: EIX) is one of the nation’s largest electric utility holding companies, focused on providing clean and reliable energy and energy services through its independent companies. Headquartered in Rosemead, California, Edison International is the parent company of Southern California Edison Company, a utility delivering electricity to 15 million people across Southern, Central and Coastal California.

Partnership with global snacking leader will help accelerate Undercover's growth, innovation and reach while preserving the entrepreneurial culture that has driven the brand's success

EAST HANOVER, N.J., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Undercover Snacks, the innovative better-for-you snack company known for its delicious chocolate-covered and frosted quinoa crisps, today announced a majority investment by Mondelēz International, one of the world's largest snacking companies.

The investment marks an exciting new stage of growth for Undercover, positioning the company to capitalize on growing consumer demand for delicious, better-for-you snacks and permissible indulgence.

Undercover began as an entrepreneurial startup and has grown into a nationally recognized brand sold in more than 25,000 retail locations and enjoyed by millions of travelers each month on United Airlines. The company will continue to operate as a standalone business led by its existing management team, while gaining access to Mondelēz's extensive capabilities, resources and expertise to accelerate innovation, distribution and long-term growth.

Undercover was founded in 2016 after Diana Levy set out to create a delicious better-for-you snack for her family following the diagnosis of two of her three teen-aged daughters with celiac disease. What began in Diana's kitchen, developed into an entirely new kind of snackable treat: crispy quinoa lightly covered in premium chocolate, combining indulgent taste and irresistible crunch with simple, high-quality ingredients that happen to be gluten-free. Undercover has continued to expand the concept with new flavors and formats while remaining true to its promise of delivering "healthy ingredients in disguise."

"We are incredibly excited to partner with Mondelēz and begin the next stage of Undercover's journey," said Diana Levy, Founder and CEO of Undercover Snacks. "When I first started making chocolate quinoa crisps in my kitchen, I was simply trying to create a snack that my entire family could enjoy. I never imagined how far that idea would go. We now have an extraordinary team, which includes my husband and three daughters, products that consumers genuinely love and an opportunity to build Undercover into something much bigger. Mondelēz shares our passion for great-tasting snacks and brings world-class capabilities that can help us innovate faster, reach many more consumers and build Undercover into a major global brand — while enabling us to preserve the culture, entrepreneurial spirit and passion for simple, high-quality ingredients that make Undercover special."

Undercover has grown rapidly with strong distribution across grocery, mass, club, drug, foodservice and e-commerce channels. Its products are sold at leading retailers including Whole Foods Market, Target, Walmart, Kroger, CVS, Walgreens, Sprouts and Albertsons, as well as Amazon and UndercoverSnacks.com. Undercover has also gained extraordinary trial and brand recognition through its longstanding relationship with United Airlines, which has handed out over 175 million units since 2023 as one of its complimentary main-cabin snacks.

"From the beginning, we believed Undercover's uniquely delicious and innovative products gave us the potential to build a major brand in the snacking industry," said Michael Levy, Executive Chairman and lead investor of Undercover Snacks. "We made significant investments in building a state-of-the-art production facility and our own quinoa crisping operation, establishing proprietary capabilities to fuel our growth. Mondelēz is an extraordinary partner to help us realize that potential. Combining its world-class capabilities in sales, distribution, marketing, procurement and consumer insights with Undercover's innovative products, entrepreneurial culture and passionate team creates tremendous opportunities to accelerate our growth and bring Undercover to consumers around the world."

Undercover will operate as a standalone business within Mondelēz International's North America Ventures business unit, alongside other high-growth brands including Perfect Snacks, Tate's Bake Shop and Hu Chocolate. Diana Levy will continue to lead the Undercover team as CEO, and Michael Levy will continue to focus on the company's growth, strategy and operations as President and COO. Diana and Michael will retain a significant minority stake in Undercover and will both serve on its Board of Directors.

"This is an incredible milestone for all of us at Undercover, but we really view it as just the beginning," added Diana Levy. "Our mission remains the same: create delicious, innovative, better-for-you snacks that people genuinely love. What changes is the scale of the opportunity in front of us. We could not be more excited about what we can build together."

Centerview Partners served as exclusive financial advisor to Undercover, and Goodwin Procter LLP served as legal counsel, with the Goodwin team led by Ilan Nissan, Jonathan Scott and Jack Kelly.

About Undercover Snacks

Undercover Snacks is an innovative better-for-you snack company creating delicious treats with "healthy ingredients in disguise." Its signature chocolate and frosted quinoa crisps combine irresistible taste and crunch with simple, high-quality ingredients. All Undercover products are non-gmo, certified gluten-free and produced at the company's dedicated peanut-free, tree-nut-free facility in East Hanover, New Jersey. Undercover is committed to sustainable sourcing, uses Rainforest Alliance-certified cocoa, and manufactures in a facility powered by solar energy.

Available in more than 25,000 retail locations nationwide, online and aboard United Airlines, Undercover has built a loyal following among consumers looking for a delicious and more permissible way to indulge. For more information, visit UndercoverSnacks.com.

Mondelēz International, Inc. (Nasdaq: MDLZ) empowers people to snack right in over 150 countries around the world. With 2025 net revenues of approximately $38.5 billion, MDLZ is leading the future of snacking with iconic global and local brands such as Oreo, Ritz, LU, Clif Bar and Tate's Bake Shop biscuits and baked snacks, as well as Cadbury Dairy Milk, Milka and Toblerone chocolate. IBTN reports Revenue growth of 12% Y/Y for 3Q26; Declares cash dividend of $0.12 for 4Q26

NASHVILLE, Tenn., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, InsCorp, Inc. (OTCQX: IBTN) reported results for the third quarter ("3Q26") ended September 30, 2026. Fully diluted earnings per share ("EPS") of $0.73 in 3Q26 compared to $0.72 in 2Q26 and $0.76 in 3Q25; excluding the benefit associated with a federal tax credit purchase in 3Q25, EPS was $0.66 in 3Q25. Balance sheet growth remained solid during the quarter as average earning asset growth of 13% Y/Y reflected average loan growth of 14% Y/Y and average deposit growth of 9% Y/Y. Excluding growth associated with the strategic entry into Murfreesboro in 3Q25, average earning assets, loans, and deposits increased 8%, 7%, and 4% Y/Y, respectively, in 3Q26. InsCorp's ROA of 0.80%, ROATCE of 10.78%, and efficiency ratio of 64.44% in 3Q26 compared to respective levels of 0.81%, 10.97%, and 64.83%, in 2Q26, and 0.93%, 11.29%, and 64.72%, in 3Q25. "While volatility seems to define financial markets this year, we're pleased to report the bank continues to experience steady growth, margin stability, and healthy measures of risk metrics—the boring things that allow tangible book value growth to compound over time," said President and CEO Jim Rieniets. "With regard to the third quarter, increased operating leverage and pre-provision, pretax income were the manifestations of investments in personnel, new markets, and technologies over the last several quarters," Rieniets continued.

New client deposit and loan growth in Murfreesboro continued in 3Q26. Deposit and loan balances attributed to the Murfreesboro team were $55.8 million and $67.6 million at 3Q26-end compared to $36.3 million and $50.3 million at 2Q26-end, and $27.5 million and $22.9 million at 4Q25-end. The Murfreesboro expansion affected EPS by ($0.02) in 3Q26 compared to $0.01 in 2Q26, ($0.06) in 1Q26, and ($0.15) in 2025. The linked-quarter ("LQ") decline was primarily due to timing of loan growth and provision expense, which occurred late in 3Q26. The end of period ("EOP") earning asset base was supportive of continued improvement in pre-provision, pretax income. Noninterest bearing and money market balances increased LQ and represented 84% of the deposits attributable to the Murfreesboro team's efforts. "This quarter effectively marked our first full year of operations in Rutherford County, and the results our team has produced should make our stakeholders proud," said Billie Jo Parker, Chief Banking Officer. "Beyond impressive growth and performance metrics, the integration of operations and the confluence of cultures finds us bullish on our future prospects in Murfreesboro," Parker continued.  

Growth in revenue of 12% Y/Y and overhead 11% Y/Y in 3Q26 resulted in pre-provision pretax income ("PPNR") growth of 12% Y/Y to $3.1 million in 3Q26. PPNR improved 20% annualized in the quarter, as expense growth represented 51% of revenue growth between 3Q26 and 2Q26 and 64% on a Y/Y basis. Net interest income growth of 12% Y/Y and 9% LQA in 3Q26 was largely responsible for revenue growth in the quarter. The increase in noninterest income of 8% Y/Y to $455,000 was driven by a 42% increase in deposit account service charges to $121,000 in 3Q26.

Noninterest expense growth of 11% Y/Y and LQA reflected an increase in personnel expense of 12% Y/Y (18% LQA) in 3Q26. Although associate growth slowed to one FTE in 3Q26 vs. 2Q26, the timing of new hires later in 2Q26 contributed more meaningfully to overhead expense in 3Q26 than in 2Q26. Excluding costs related to the Murfreesboro expansion, noninterest expense growth was 7% Y/Y in 3Q26. Noninterest expense was 2.09% of average assets in 3Q26 versus 2.06% in 2Q26 and 2.12% in 1Q25; excluding costs associated with the Murfreesboro expansion, the ratio was 1.99% in 3Q26 compared to 1.96% in 2Q26 and 2.10% in 3Q25. "On multiple fronts we have visibility to greater operating leverage and efficiencies over the next couple years," said Scott Gupton, Chief Operating Officer. "While recent quarters saw the bank solidifying its personnel foundation in strategically important areas, those additions will ensure sustainable growth while leaders across the organization integrate artificial intelligence to scale productivity across the company," Gupton continued.    

Average earning asset growth of 13%, or $121 million, Y/Y primarily consisted of average loan growth of 14%, or $112 million, Y/Y in 3Q26. On an end of period basis ("EOP"), loan growth of 17% Y/Y (15% LQA) reflected contributions from commercial real estate ("CRE"), construction & development ("C&D"), home equity ("HELOC"), and commercial & industrial ("C&I") loans in 3Q26. Growth in C&I (14% Y/Y; -3% LQA), CRE (13% Y/Y; 14% LQA), C&D (44% YY; 29% LQA), and residential (26% Y/Y; 45% LQ), largely due to HELOC growth, drove growth in 3Q26. Medquity, INSBANK's healthcare division, originated $29 million of loans in 3Q26 compared to $15 million in 2Q26 and an average of $33 million over the trailing twelve months. Net of payoffs and participations sold, Medquity's portfolio grew 17% Y/Y (flat LQ) in 3Q26. Excluding Medquity's loan balances (28% of loans), loan growth was 17% Y/Y (21% LQ) in 3Q26. "Our healthcare portfolio remains a unique line of business which leverages the expertise of our team to serve a nationwide market of industry providers," said Blake Wilson, President of Medquity. "Given the scope and relative stability of healthcare spending in the US, we believe continued focus on scaling Medquity can support growth objectives while minimizing correlation of risks with other asset concentrations such as CRE," Wilson continued.

Deposit growth of 14% Y/Y reflected interest-bearing transaction balance growth of 64% Y/Y in 3Q26. Non-maturity deposit balances, which include noninterest bearing, interest-bearing demand, and money market balances, increased 46% Y/Y, lifting the mix to 54% of deposits, up from 49% a quarter ago and 42% a year ago. "Growing non-maturity and relationship deposits remain an important part of strengthening the bank's funding profile," stated Andrew Smith, Chief Deposit Officer. "By deepening customer relationships and capturing a greater share of their deposits, we are building a more efficient funding base that supports margin performance and interest rate risk management," Smith continued. CD balance growth of -10% Y/Y and -11% LQ in 3Q26 resulted in a mix of 46% of deposits, down from 51% a quarter ago and 58% a year ago. The loan-to-deposit ratio was 100% versus 97% a year ago.

INSBANK's sensitivity to future changes in interest rates was largely neutral at 3Q26-end. Continued improvement in the mix of non-maturity deposits to total deposits and some usage of interest rate derivatives were largely responsible for the reduction in sensitivity over the past two years. This change reflects that INSBANK's asset and liability re-pricing mismatch is short-lived and largely resolved within three months of a change in the Fed Funds rate. "Market-based interest rates advanced faster and more meaningfully than the Fed Funds rate in YTD26, which offset the positive effect of low-yielding loans that re-priced higher in the first nine months of the year," stated Peyton Green, Chief Financial Officer. "Although our modeling reflects a slight benefit to the margin in 4Q26 from the increase in the Fed Funds rate in September, the lag in policy rates compared to market rates will likely neutralize that benefit," concluded Green. The net interest margin ("NIM") of 3.18% in 3Q26 compared to 3.18% in 2Q26 and 3.20% in 3Q25. The loan yield was 6.56% in 3Q26 vs. 6.64% in 2Q26 and 6.79% in 3Q25. The cost of deposits and cost of funds improved 15 bps and 17 bps Y/Y, respectively, to 3.21% and 3.32% in 3Q26.

Asset quality remained strong in 3Q26. Net chargeoffs ("NCOs") represented 0.00% of average loans on an annualized basis in 3Q26, 2Q26, 3Q25. Nonperforming loans and 90-day past dues ("NPLs") represented 0.32% of loans, as of 3Q26-end vs. 0.25% a quarter ago and 0.84% a year ago. Loans 30-89 days past due represented 0.12% of loans at 3Q26-end compared to 0.28% a quarter ago and 0.19% a year ago. The allowance for credit losses of 1.25% of loans (-9 bps Y/Y) represented 394% of NPLs.

INSBANK maintained solid capital cushions above "Well Capitalized" regulatory capital thresholds. Specifically, the tier-1 leverage, common equity tier-1 capital, and total risk-based capital ratios were 10.21%, 10.83%, and 12.02%, respectively, at quarter-end. InsCorp, Inc.'s tangible common equity ratio was 7.04% as of 3Q26-end vs. 8.14% a year ago. Tangible book value per share decreased 1% Y/Y to $26.20, as of September 30, 2026. C&D and CRE balances represented 85% and 328% of total risk-based capital, respectively, versus 62% and 292% a year ago. Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income was ($5.4 million), or 4.9% of bank-level Tier 1 capital of $111.5 million, as of September 30, 2026.

Final round of PG&E Corporation Foundation grants completes a five-year, $2.5 million investment in 25 community organizations

Link to the B-roll and soundbite from Sacramento Splash

OAKLAND, Calif., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The PG&E Corporation Foundation (PG&E Foundation) is awarding five community-based organizations in Northern and Central California a total of $500,000 in grants for local initiatives dedicated to environmental stewardship.

The 2026 grant recipients represent the program's final group, completing the PG&E Foundation's five-year investment in projects that help strengthen local ecosystems and communities.

Since its launch in 2022, the Better Together Nature Positive Innovation Grant Program has invested $2.5 million in 25 organizations across Pacific Gas and Electric Company's (PG&E) service area, advancing environmental stewardship and supporting community-led innovation.

The five organizations will each receive $100,000 through the Better Together Nature Positive Innovation Grant program for leading efforts to preserve California's unique biodiversity, focusing on land, air quality and water stewardship.

Funding for this initiative comes from PG&E shareholders, not customers.

"For 27 years, Sacramento Splash has helped kids connect with the natural world through hands-on science and environmental education. Thanks to PG&E's support, about 7,000 students will experience Project Agriculture, Water, Energy & Environment during the 2026–27 school year, learning where their food comes from and how everyday choices can help create a more sustainable future," said Mackenzie Wieser, Chief Executive Officer, Sacramento Splash.

"We extend our sincere gratitude to all the organizations, partners and community leaders who helped make this program a success. What inspires us most is seeing local organizations turn their deep understanding of their communities into meaningful action, creating lasting impact where it matters most," said Carla Peterman, President, PG&E Corporation, and Chair of The PG&E Corporation Foundation Board.

Grant recipients are based in each of PG&E's five regions: North Coast; North Valley and Sierra; Bay Area; South Bay and Central Coast; and Central Valley. Receiving grants are:

  • Noyo Center: Kelp Forest Recovery (Fort Bragg) - Noyo Center restores Mendocino Coast kelp forests by removing invasive urchins and planting bull kelp. The project also supports red abalone recovery and environmental education. These efforts help create healthier, more resilient coastal ecosystems.
  • Sacramento Splash (Sacramento) - Project Agriculture, Water, Energy & Environment gives students in grades 2-5 from underserved Sacramento County schools hands-on learning experiences at the Historic Nicolaus Dairy in Elk Grove, often providing their first opportunity to visit a working farm. Students explore agriculture and environmental stewardship by planting and harvesting crops, building compost, observing bees, and learning about water conservation. Grant funding will support educators, transportation for Title I schools, and educational materials, helping the program reach approximately 7,000 students from 231 classes during the 2026-27 school year.
  • Friends of Sausal Creek (Oakland) - Friends of Sausal Creek will expand its paid youth stewardship program to provide year-round green job skills training for Oakland youth while helping restore the 2,600-acre Sausal Creek watershed. Participants will gain hands-on experience through habitat restoration, water quality improvements, and kayak-based estuary cleanups. In Jingletown, youth will also design and install a native planting plan and help create a community interpretive sign.
  • Point Blue Conservation Science (Bolinas) - Point Blue Conservation Science's program gives K-12 students hands-on experience restoring natural habitats while learning about environmental stewardship. In San Benito County, students, community college interns, residents, and land stewards will work with local partners to plant native vegetation and restore streamside habitat along an important wildlife corridor. The project will improve water quality, wildlife habitat, and climate resilience while providing students with education, job training and career development opportunities in conservation.
  • Black Urban Farmers Association (Stockton) – Black Urban Farmers Association (BUFA) has operated a pesticide-free urban farm in Stockton since 2015, providing fresh food and promoting regenerative farming. The project will help BUFA expand to a permanent one-acre site with more green space, education, and sustainable agriculture opportunities. Grant funding will support site planning, environmental reviews, infrastructure, and a community launch, strengthening long-term food security and environmental stewardship.

With the selection of the 2026 grantees, the application period has closed and the Better Together Nature Positive Innovation Grant Program is no longer accepting applications.

The PG&E Corporation Foundation is an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, separate from PG&E and sponsored by PG&E Corporation.

  • Joby begins a week-long series of flights across Florida with its all-electric vertical lift air taxi, in partnership with the Florida Department of Transportation
  • Flights are part of the White House-backed eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP), accelerating the safe introduction of electric air taxis across the U.S.
  • Campaign opens with a historic flight across Tampa Bay from downtown St. Petersburg to Tampa International Airport, retracing the world’s first scheduled commercial airline route

TAMPA, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Joby Aviation, Inc. (NYSE: JOBY) today launches a week of piloted electric air taxi flights across Florida, taking its aircraft from Tampa to Orlando and on to the Space Coast. The aircraft will fly at Orlando International Airport and Kennedy Space Center, helping map the first phase of Florida’s planned Aerial Highway Network. These are Florida’s first flights under the White House-backed eIPP program, announced by the U.S. Department of Transportation in March 2026. The program brings government and industry together to accelerate the safe introduction of electric air taxis into U.S. airspace.

Joby’s vertical lift electric air taxi flies over Tampa, Florida, on Thursday, Oct. 29, ahead of the state’s first eIPP flights (Photo: Joby Aviation)

Florida is where commercial aviation began more than a century ago, and this week it once again takes center stage as Joby launches its statewide flight campaign with a historic journey across Tampa Bay. The flight from downtown St. Petersburg to Tampa International Airport retraces the route flown on January 1, 1914, when aviation pioneer Tony Jannus carried former St. Petersburg Mayor Abe Pheil across the bay on the world’s first scheduled commercial airline flight. Floridians will have a front-row seat to the next chapter in aviation history as Joby brings its electric air taxi to the same skies. The milestone will be celebrated at Albert Whitted Park, where residents, families, tourists and aviation enthusiasts are invited to gather and watch the aircraft take flight and be part of a new moment in Florida’s aviation history.

The Florida Department of Transportation’s (FDOT) project was one of eight selected nationwide and is a statewide effort with multiple industry partners, planned in three phases covering passenger transportation, cargo delivery, automation and medical response.

Florida has been preparing for this moment for years, FDOT has led statewide Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) planning since 2021. In April 2026, Gov. Ron DeSantis signed House Bill 1093, which allows FDOT to fund vertiport infrastructure statewide. FDOT is also building SunTrax Air, a dedicated AAM test campus off Interstate 4 that is home to the nation’s first dedicated AAM aerial test track, where AAM testing is planned to begin by the end of 2026. Together they make Florida an attractive place for Joby to operate, and this week’s eIPP flights are the first step toward commercial service in the state.

Throughout the week, Joby will fly in the first planned hubs of Florida’s Aerial Highway Network, the state’s planned intercity air taxi system*:

  • Tampa Bay: Point-to-point flight on Oct. 30 from Albert Whitted Airport (SPG) in downtown St. Petersburg to Tampa International Airport (TPA). Community members are invited to watch the takeoff and a live stream of the flight from Albert Whitted Park beginning at 8:45 a.m., at a community event hosted by the City of St. Petersburg celebrating the world’s first scheduled commercial airline flight.
  • Orlando: Flight at Orlando International Airport (MCO) landing near the airport’s Terminal C and Train Station at a new vertiport, a dedicated eVTOL landing site, flown on routes and enabled by procedures developed over two years of simulation with the FAA, NASA, the Greater Orlando Aviation Authority and Orlando air traffic controllers.
  • Kennedy Space Center: Flight at the Shuttle Landing Facility during the UP.Summit, bringing the aircraft to the home of American spaceflight before industry leaders where the country’s aerospace ambitions launched more than 60 years ago.

*Schedule subject to change based on weather conditions and other factors.

“More than a century ago, Florida made history with the world’s first commercial airline flight. Today, Florida is helping lead the next generation in aviation,” said JoeBen Bevirt, founder and CEO of Joby. “From Tampa Bay to Orlando and the Space Coast, we're giving Floridians a glimpse of a future where quiet, all-electric aircraft make it easier and faster to connect the places people live, work and visit. Florida has the vision, the destinations and the ambition to lead this transformation, and we're proud to work alongside FDOT to turn that vision into reality.”

“Florida is helping safely integrate these new aircraft into the airspace system and prove that the next great era of American aviation is already here,” said FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford. “Each flight provides crucial data and lessons learned that will help establish safety standards for everyday operations.”

“More than 100 years ago, Florida helped launch the commercial aviation industry. Today, we are helping shape the next era of flight,” said Florida Department of Transportation Secretary Jared W. Perdue, P.E. “Through strategic investments, statewide planning, and partnerships with some of the industry’s top innovators, Florida is creating the infrastructure and policies needed to safely integrate Advanced Air Mobility into our transportation system. These flights demonstrate how we are turning vision into reality.”

Joby’s commitment to Florida predates this week’s flights. Blade, Joby’s wholly owned subsidiary, has flown passengers between the New York area and South Florida since 2015 and will relaunch its BLADEone jet service to Miami and Palm Beach in November in partnership with private jet airline Aero. This service gives Joby an established customer base, ground infrastructure and experience in the state as it prepares to introduce electric air taxi service.

Florida is the final stop on Joby’s 2026 Electric Skies Tour, a nationwide showcase celebrating the United States’ 250th anniversary, following flights in the San Francisco Bay Area, New York, Dallas-Fort Worth and ending at Kennedy Space Center. As Joby continues to move through the final stages of FAA type certification, the eIPP flight campaign provides the FAA and state partners with critical operational data on airport integration, acoustics and vertiport procedures ahead of commercial launch.

Joby Aviation, Inc. (NYSE: JOBY) is a next-generation aviation company based in California. Its aircraft, propulsion and autonomy technologies span both commercial aviation and defense applications. Joby also operates Blade, a leading urban air mobility business providing passenger transportation services in the United States and Europe. Joby intends to operate its fast, quiet and convenient air taxi service in cities around the world and sell its aircraft to other operators and partners. To learn more, visit www.jobyaviation.com.

GREENSBURG, Pa., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- To help strengthen housing stability and support vulnerable communities, the FirstEnergy Foundation is investing $115,000 in 14 Pennsylvania organizations that provide critical housing assistance and supportive services to individuals and families facing homelessness, domestic violence and other housing-related challenges.

Among the Pennsylvania recipients is the Blackburn Center, which has served survivors and victims of domestic violence and other crimes in Westmoreland County for nearly 50 years. The $5,000 grant will help support shelter operations, basic necessities and vital programs that provide safety, support and resources for individuals and families during times of crisis.

John Hawkins, President, FirstEnergy Pennsylvania: "The Blackburn Center provides a lifeline for individuals and families facing some of life's most difficult circumstances," said Hawkins. "For nearly 50 years, the organization has delivered safe shelter, compassionate support and critical resources to those in need throughout Westmoreland County. We're proud to support that mission."

In addition to the grant, FirstEnergy Pennsylvania employees at the Greensburg Corporate Center and the Jeannette and Latrobe service centers organized a donation drive to collect many of the shelter's most-needed items.

Renee Reitz, Executive Director, Blackburn Center: "Blackburn Center is incredibly grateful for this generous donation and FirstEnergy's support of our mission. The items will help meet the needs of the individuals and families we serve, while the financial contribution will support our clients and help sustain our emergency shelter program. We sincerely appreciate the generosity and the difference it makes in our community."

In addition to the Blackburn Center, the following Pennsylvania organizations were also awarded grants:

General Shelters

  • Opportunity House (Berks County)
  • Hope Rescue Mission (Berks County)
  • Housing Transitions (Centre County)
  • Valley Youth House (Northampton County)

Domestic Violence Shelters

  • Safe Berks (Berks County)
  • Family Services Inc. (Blair County)
  • SafeNet Erie (Erie County)
  • AWARE, Inc. (Mercer County)
  • Women's Resources of Monroe County, Inc., DBA Safe Monroe (Monroe County)
  • Bloom for Women (Northampton County)
  • Third Street Alliance for Women and Children (Northampton County)
  • A Safe Place (Warren County)
  • YWCA York (York County)

Supporting Organizations That Provide Safety and Stability

The Pennsylvania grants are part of FirstEnergy Foundation's expanded Shelter, Safety and Stability initiative, which supports organizations across FirstEnergy's five-state service territory that provide emergency shelter, transitional housing and critical support services for individuals and families facing homelessness, housing insecurity and domestic violence. The Foundation increased funding for the initiative fivefold this year, expanding support from $100,000 to $500,000.

Since 2020, the FirstEnergy Foundation has donated over $1.6 million to help people in need of shelter or a place to call home. Nearly $700,000 of that was directed specifically to organizations that support domestic violence survivors and their families.

About FirstEnergy Foundation

The FirstEnergy Foundation supports 501(c)(3) organizations across FirstEnergy's operational area, helping them build capacity, strengthen outcomes and deliver lasting impact. Giving priorities include housing stability, hunger relief, workforce development and STEM initiatives that reflect community needs and the company's strategic focus. Including the Shelter, Safety and Stability initiative, the Foundation has distributed more than $6.5 million in community support across FirstEnergy's service area to date in 2026.

Its electric distribution companies form one of the nation's largest investor-owned electric systems, serving more than 6 million customers in Ohio, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, West Virginia, Maryland and New York. The company's transmission subsidiaries operate approximately 24,000 miles of transmission lines that connect the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic regions.
